official_sources.title: Planning Data documentation and API reference

verified_claims: The Planning Data API exposes more than 100 England planning and housing datasets through one interface.
Coordinate queries require latitude and longitude and return entities whose geometries cover the point.
Multiple dataset filters can be supplied in a single entity request.
UPRN values can be queried through the q parameter and are described as more precise than coordinates for registered properties.
Entity records can include name, dataset, start-date, geometry and point fields.
Geometry and point values are represented as WKT in entity responses.
An absence of results is not proof that no constraint exists because coverage varies by area.
geometry_entity can reuse an existing entity geometry instead of embedding a raw polygon.
The single-entity endpoint requires an integer entity identifier and json, html or geojson extension.
The platform publishes an OpenAPI document for generated clients.
Planning geometry specifications require WGS84 coordinates.
CSV geometry is supplied as WKT while GeoJSON, GML and GeoPackage use their associated geometry formats.
Permanent unique references and entry dates are part of published dataset lineage controls.
Planning records do not by themselves prove the three candidates' current HMLR identity or measured elevation.
